record.paper_title: Billiard dynamics: A survey with the emphasis on open problems
record.original_question: Is every semi-dispersing billiard table hyperbolic? Here a semi-dispersing billiard table is a planar billiard table whose boundary consists of smooth inward-convex dispersing arcs together with some neutral straight components.

evidence.quote: Задача 4. i) Будет ли произвольный полурассеивающий биллиардный стол гиперболическим?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A planar billiard table is a compact connected region $Q\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ whose boundary $\partial Q$ is a finite union of $C^\infty$ arcs meeting at finitely many corner points. The billiard flow on $Q$ is defined by free unit-speed motion in the interior of $Q$ together with elastic reflection at smooth boundary points (the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection). An arc of $\partial Q$ is called dispersing if it is curved and inward-convex (i.e., the region $Q$ lies on the concave side of the arc, so that the arc's curvature, oriented inward to $Q$, is strictly positive); it is called neutral if it is a straight line segment. 

Call $Q$ a semi-dispersing billiard table if every smooth component of $\partial Q$ is either a dispersing arc or a neutral straight segment, and at least one dispersing arc occurs.

The billiard map $T$ is defined on the set of unit tangent vectors based at smooth boundary points of $Q$ and pointing inward, taking each such vector to the next reflection. Equip this phase space with the canonical invariant probability measure $\mu$. The system $(T,\mu)$ is called hyperbolic if both Lyapunov exponents of $T$ are nonzero $\mu$-almost everywhere.

Question: Is every semi-dispersing planar billiard table, in the sense above, hyperbolic?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether every planar semi-dispersing billiard table is hyperbolic appears to remain open. While hyperbolicity is established under additional assumptions (e.g., absence of degenerate geometric configurations, or specific cone-field arguments such as Wojtkowski's principle), surveys on billiard dynamics list it as an open problem, and related questions about adding focusing perturbations to semi-dispersing billiards explicitly note that hyperbolicity is conjectural but not proved in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Recent advances in open billiards with some open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing open problems on hyperbolicity of billiards including semi-dispersing settings.
status_evidence.claim: The hyperbolicity of general semi-dispersing billiards is discussed as an open/partially understood problem.

status_evidence.title: Hard Ball Systems and Semi-Dispersive Billiards: Hyperbolicity and Ergodicity
status_evidence.snippet: Research focuses on proving full hyperbolicity (nonzero Lyapunov exponents almost everywhere) for semi-dispersive billiards.
status_evidence.claim: Full hyperbolicity for semi-dispersing billiards is an active research problem and not established in full generality.
